CAT.rationale: CAT's fundamental health is strong — revenue +22.2% YoY, EPS +30.2% YoY, ROE 50.5%, $51B record backlog, and Q2 2026 earnings 'smashing estimates' per headlines on the decision date. However, the valuation pillar is extremely unfavorable: P/E has expanded from ~20x to ~46x in twelve months (91st percentile of 1-year range) while net margin actually declined from 15.7% to 13.3%. The 2.2% earnings yield is less than half the 4.54% 10-year Treasury yield, leaving no margin of safety. P/B at 23.4x (88th percentile) and P/S at 30-year highs per Michael Burry's short thesis further confirm extreme overvaluation. Gross margin compressed from 37.1% to 35.1% YoY, and Resource Industries segment profit plunged 39% with 700bp margin compression. Tariff headwinds of $2.2-2.4B for 2026 and a narrowing yield curve (T10Y2Y=0.38%) add cyclical risk. The Q2 earnings beat is a near-term positive (pillar 3), but it cannot rescue a case where the stock has already priced in perfection — the market is paying 2.3x the historical multiple for a business with compressing margins. Multiple compression is the dominant risk: reversion from 46x to even 30x PE implies ~35% downside holding earnings flat. This is a quality franchise at an unsustainable price.
